title: Recording with Morton in Chicago
summary: Morton wrote music for the records, which Ory says were not rehearsed much.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. He came in Los Angeles, I had a pole battle, you know, as a funeral, you remember. Yeah. Yeah. He wanted to organize a band, he'd actually play, but he didn't have anything to offer.
Yeah. But you made a lot of records with him in Chicago. Yeah. But they weren't the well rehearsed jobs. You didn't rehearse those much either? No. Did he have any music at those record days?

Yeah, music. He told me, not worry about my part, but I played what he wrote for me and he, I know some of them, they don't sound like you, they forget to turn that over. Uh-huh. But you guys played what you see. So some of them. He told Simmy too, you know. Uh-huh. To go for himself. Yeah. Spot, you know. He told me no way about it. I can't write your music. Uh-huh. Were those silk shirts white colored or? Different colored. Most they colored, you know, striped. Bright colored? Yeah. Yeah. One rang the other day and she grabbed her shoes and said, this is Mr. Babad Ory.
